query: What factors explain low review scores?

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a strong grouping axis to compare low-score rates across product types; well-populated and non-trivial. Sample categorizations (pet_food_treat, snack, candy, beverage) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: brew_strength_complaint
per_column.rationale: A specific complaint dimension relevant to a large coffee/tea segment, giving a real axis for explaining low scores within that segment. Values are correctly 'not_applicable' for non-brew items in samples, appropriately silent-handling.

per_column.name: palatability_rejection
per_column.rationale: Taste/refusal is a plausible driver of low scores and offers a graded axis (full/partial/refused). Sample values match text (positive reviews = full_acceptance; medicinal-flavor and mislabel cases = not_applicable is defensible).

per_column.name: product_freshness_staleness
per_column.rationale: Staleness is a genuine potential cause of low scores; though heavily skewed (171 true), it still isolates a meaningful failure mode. Sample values (all false for reviews not mentioning staleness) are correct.

per_column.name: product_performance_failure
per_column.rationale: Graded failure/adverse-effect axis directly targets reasons for dissatisfaction. Sample readings are consistent with text (positive/neutral reviews = no_failure).

per_column.name: fulfillment_service_failure
per_column.rationale: Shipping/service problems are a well-known driver of low scores independent of product quality, so this is a useful distinct axis. However, the mislabeled 'Not as Advertised' peanuts row arguably reflects a fulfillment/vendor issue yet is marked false; still defensible as a labeling vs. shipping distinction.

per_column.name: ingredient_transparency_concern
per_column.rationale: Captures labeling/ingredient concerns that can explain complaints. Skewed but non-trivial. The 'Not as Advertised' row could plausibly be true here yet is false, a minor grounding softness, but no invented facts observed in samples.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a coherent set of complaint/failure-mode axes plus a product-category grouping, all directly relevant to explaining low review scores and offering genuine axes to group and model on. None are trivial constants or mere restatements of Score/Summary. Values in the row-evidence samples are sound readings of the source text, with appropriate not_applicable/false handling for silent rows and no invented facts; only minor debatable calls (e.g., mislabeled peanuts not flagged as fulfillment/transparency) slightly soften groundedness.
